transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me, I really appreciate it. Um... I guess they brought me in because of some things at the warehouse where I work. I move freight and, well, I try to do a really good job, I promise. But... I guess I've been doing some things that upset the supervisor? I didn't mean to. 

Like, sometimes I'll just sort of freeze by the forklift with my arms up in the air. And I was copying the beeping sounds it makes, and the hand signals the drivers use... I thought I was just sort of joining in, you know? Is that okay? But they got really mad because I was also moving the boxes into these... strange little patterns. Even when everyone was yelling for me to stop, I just kept doing it. I really didn't mean to cause any trouble or bother anyone. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Do you often find yourself repeating certain actions or movements outside of work as well?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I try to be really normal when I'm at home or out, you know? I don't want people to think I'm weird or anything. 

Sometimes I guess I might... like, arrange my shoes in a certain way, or maybe tap my fingers a little bit if I'm watching TV, but that's just normal fidgeting, right? Everyone does that, don't they? I really try my best to just fit in and be good. I hope that's the right answer... I don't want to make it sound like I'm doing bad things all the time. Is that what you meant?
Do you ever have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to stop thinking about them?

Um, no... not really. I mean, I try to keep my mind pretty clear, you know? I don't really get stuck on things. 

Sometimes I might think about work a little bit after I clock out, like if I remembered I put a box in the wrong spot, but that's just caring about my job, right? I want to be a good employee. I don't have bad thoughts or weird things stuck in my head, I promise. I usually just try to think about nice things, or whatever is on the TV. I hope that's okay? I'm trying to give you the right answer.
Do you find it hard to make friends or understand what others are thinking or feeling?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I think I'm pretty good at getting along with people. I always try to be friendly and polite, you know? 

I have friends from... well, from high school and some from my college classes before I started at the warehouse. We don't hang out all the time, but everybody's just really busy, right? That's normal for guys my age. And at work, I try to smile and nod when people talk to me. I don't want to bother them, so I mostly keep to myself, but that just means I'm a hard worker, right? I'm not trying to be difficult or anything. I hope I'm making sense. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you ever feel like you have to follow certain rules or rituals when you're interacting with other people?

Um, no... no, I don't think so. I mean, I just try to be polite, like I said. 

I guess I try to make sure I don't look people in the eye for too long, because I read once that it can make people uncomfortable, and I really don't want to make anyone uncomfortable. So I might, like, look at their shoulder or the floor sometimes. But that's just being respectful of their space, right? It's not a weird rule or anything like that. I just want people to think I'm a nice guy. Is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm not doing it wrong.
Do you have any hobbies or activities that you enjoy doing in your free time that you find yourself doing over and over?

Um, no, not really over and over. I mean, I like normal things, you know? 

I play video games sometimes, or watch YouTube videos about... well, just normal stuff, like video games or movies. I might rewatch a video if I really liked it, or if I missed something the first time, but that's just because I want to pay attention, right? I'm not doing it in a weird way. I just like to relax after my shift at the warehouse because my feet get pretty tired. I try to stay busy with good, normal hobbies so I don't get lazy. Does that sound like a good answer? I'm trying to be helpful.
Do you feel like your behaviors, such as arranging boxes in certain patterns or copying sounds, cause you any problems or distress?

Um, problems? No, no, they don't cause me any problems. I mean, the boxes... that's just me trying to do a really good job at the warehouse, you know? 

I just like things to be neat. If I put them in a certain way, it just looks better, and it helps me focus. My supervisor hasn't complained or anything, so it must be okay, right? And the sounds... well, sometimes I just repeat things I hear because it helps me remember them, or just to make sure I heard it right. It's not like a big deal or anything that bothers me. I'm just trying to be careful and do things the right way. I really hope that doesn't sound bad... I'm just trying to be a good worker. Is that what you were asking?
Do you think your behaviors at work, like arranging boxes in patterns, are affecting your relationships with your coworkers or your ability to do your job?

Um, well... I mean, I don't think it's a big deal, really. I'm just trying to be careful, like I said. But, um... I guess maybe some people don't see it that way? 

Like, they took me off the forklift duties recently. I think they just wanted someone else to have a turn, but my supervisor said something about keeping things safe around me. And, um, I haven't been going to my community college classes as much... I just fell a little behind because I was trying to make sure everything at work was perfect, you know? And I used to help out at the church food bank, but I stopped showing up for my shifts there, too. They said they couldn't count on me anymore, which really hurts because I just want to be helpful. I'm still a good worker, though, right? I'm just trying to make sure everything is exactly right so nobody gets mad at me. Does that make sense? I really hope I'm not doing terrible.
How do you feel when you're not allowed to arrange the boxes in your preferred pattern?

Um, well... it's fine, really. I mean, I don't get mad or anything like that. I'm not a difficult person to work with. 

If they tell me to just stack them normally, I just do it. I mean, maybe I feel a little... I don't know, a little bit uneasy for a second? Just because I know my way looks neater and it feels a bit safer to me. But it's not like I throw a fit or get really upset. I just take a deep breath and do what my supervisor wants, because I want to be a good employee and follow directions. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for them. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? I just try to be agreeable.
Do you feel anxious when you can't arrange the boxes in your preferred pattern?

Anxious? Um, no... no, I wouldn't say I get anxious. I mean, like I was saying before, maybe just a tiny bit... unsettled for a second? But definitely not anxious. 

I don't get nervous or start panicking or anything like that. I just... I just nod and do it the regular way if they ask me to. I really try to be flexible, you know? I don't want anyone to think I'm causing trouble or that I can't handle my job. I just go with the flow and do what I'm told. That's the best way to be, right? I'm just trying to be a good team player. I hope I'm answering your questions okay... I really don't want to sound like I'm making things difficult for anyone.
Do you feel like you have to arrange the boxes in a certain pattern because something bad might happen if you don't?

Oh, no... um, no, definitely not. I don't think anything bad is going to happen, like... like someone getting hurt or the roof caving in or anything. It's not like that at all. 

I'm not superstitious or... or weird about it, I promise. I just, um, I just think it looks a lot better when they're lined up right. It shows I care about my work, you know? I wouldn't want you or my boss to think I'm doing it for some strange reason. I really just want the warehouse to look nice and organized for everyone. That's a good thing for an employee to do, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing things the right way so everyone is happy with my work.
Do you feel like the boxes need to be arranged in a specific way to look symmetrical or perfect?

Symmetrical? Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? But not, like, in an obsessive way or anything. I don't need it to be absolutely perfect. 

I just... I just think it looks neat, you know? Like I'm taking pride in my work. I just try to make the stacks look even and tidy so the aisles are clear. It's not like I'm measuring them with a ruler or getting upset if one is a tiny bit off. I just want it to look professional for the supervisors. I mean, doing a neat job is what they pay me for, right? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and doing things the way a good employee should. I'm not being too particular about it, am I?
Do you feel like the boxes need to be arranged in a specific way to feel right to you?

Feel right? Um... no, I wouldn't say it's about a feeling. It's not like... like an itch I have to scratch or anything weird like that. 

I just... I just want to do what's expected of me. If they're stacked up nice and neat, then I know I did a good job for the day, and that's all it is. I don't have any strange quirks about it, I promise. I just want to be a reliable worker and make sure the warehouse looks the way the managers want it to. Does that make sense? I hope I'm being helpful with these answers... I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Do you feel like the way you arrange the boxes is related to making sure everything is orderly?

Yeah, yeah, exactly. Orderly. That's... that's all it is, really. 

I just want everything to look nice and organized so the supervisors don't have anything to complain about. It's just about being a good employee and keeping the warehouse looking sharp, you know? I don't want anyone thinking I'm slacking off or making a mess. I just want to do my job right so they're happy with me. That's a completely normal way to look at it, right? Just trying to be neat and orderly for work?
Do you feel upset when someone messes up the patterns you've made with the boxes?

Upset? Oh, no, no. I don't get upset. I mean, it's a warehouse, right? Things get moved around all the time. 

If someone bumps a stack or needs to pull a box from one of my aisles, that's just part of the job. I might, um... I might just go over and straighten it back up when they're done, just to keep it looking nice for the end-of-shift check. But I don't get mad at anyone or anything like that. I know we're all just trying to get our work done. I'm pretty easygoing about it, honestly. It's just a job, you know? I wouldn't overreact to something so small. That sounds okay, right? I'm answering these right?
Do you think your way of arranging boxes or repeating sounds has ever caused problems for you in your relationships or daily life?

Problems? Um... well, I try really hard not to let anything cause problems. I want to be a good person, you know? But... I guess... well, I want to be honest with you so I'm doing this right. 

There have been a few little hiccups lately. Nothing I can't fix, I promise! It's just... at work, they actually took me off the forklift duties. They said I wasn't keeping things safe around me anymore. Which I feel awful about, I really didn't mean to worry anyone. And, um... I guess I’ve fallen a little behind in my community-college classes, too. Just a bit. Juggling everything is just taking a little more time right now. 

And I actually stopped showing up for my volunteer shifts at the church food bank... mostly because the people there started saying they couldn't count on me anymore. That really hurt to hear, because I just want to be helpful. But I'm going to do better, I swear. I'm going to get it all sorted out so everyone is happy with me again. 

Is it okay that I told you that? I hope you don't think I'm a bad worker or a bad person... I'm really trying my best to get everything back to normal.
Do you think your behaviors, such as arranging boxes in patterns or repeating sounds, are affecting your overall well-being or ability to function in daily life?

Um... well... I guess maybe they are affecting things a little bit. Like I mentioned just before... I mean, I really didn't want to bring it up again because I don't want you to think I'm failing or anything. But, yeah... it's like I said. 

They took me off the forklift, which... I mean, they said I wasn't keeping things safe, but I'm sure I can earn that back if I just try harder. And the community college classes... I'm just a little behind, that's all. I can catch up. And... and the church food bank. I stopped going because they said they couldn't count on me anymore. 

So... I guess maybe it is affecting my daily life a little bit right now. But I promise I'm going to fix it. I'm going to get it all under control so I'm functioning perfectly again. I just want to be doing everything right. Is that... is that the kind of answer you needed? I'm sorry if it sounds like I'm not doing well, I really am trying my best.
Do you feel like your behaviors, such as arranging boxes in patterns, are causing you a lot of stress or discomfort?

Stress? Um... no, no, not at all. I don't feel uncomfortable doing it. Honestly, it... it actually kind of makes me feel better? Like things are exactly where they are supposed to be. 

The only thing that stresses me out is, you know, making people upset at work or letting down the food bank, like I mentioned before. I feel really awful about that part. But the boxes themselves, or the sounds... no, they don't cause me any pain or discomfort. I really don't want you to worry about me being overwhelmed or anything like that. I'm handling things okay in my own head, I promise. 

Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that it doesn't bother me... I just want to give you the right answer so you know I'm not doing too badly.
Do you feel like you have to arrange the boxes in a certain pattern, even if you don't want to?

Um... no, not really. I don't feel forced to do it or anything like that. It's not like a... a compulsion, if that's what you mean. 

I actually want to arrange them. Like I said, it just feels right to have them that way. It's not something I'm fighting against or wishing I could stop. I just... I do it because it makes sense to me, and it helps me feel settled. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I know sometimes people do things they don't want to do, but I promise I'm in control of it. I'm not... I'm not losing my grip on things, I swear. I just like having a system. That's normal, right?
Do you feel like the way you arrange the boxes is driven by a need to make them perfectly symmetrical?

Um... perfectly symmetrical? Oh, no... no, not necessarily. I mean, I don't really worry about making them look like a mirror image or anything like that. 

It's more just about... putting them where they belong, you know? Like they have a specific place they're supposed to go, and I just put them there. It's not about making them look pretty or perfectly even. I don't obsess over the spacing or... or get upset if they aren't perfectly aligned. I promise I'm not doing anything weird like measuring them or anything. 

I just kind of group them the way that feels right. Is... is that okay? I know some people get really stuck on things having to be perfectly symmetrical, but I'm really not like that. I'm just trying to keep things organized. That's a good thing, right?
